# Status checks

RWX reports status checks to GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Cursor Origin, and Entire when runs are triggered by events from those platforms. By default, a single status check is created for the entire run. You can customize this behavior to disable status checks, rename them, or create custom status checks that group specific tasks.

## Default status checks

By default, RWX creates a single status check that reflects the overall status of your run. The status check is prefixed with `RWX:` and includes information about the run definition file and trigger type.

To disable the default status check:

```yaml
on:
  github:
    push:
      status-checks: false

```

To provide a custom name for the default status check:

```yaml
on:
  github:
    push:
      status-checks:
        name: CI

```

This will display as `RWX: CI` on your commit.

Use the custom status check name if you rename a run definition and want the status check to match the previous status check name.

## Custom status checks

Custom status checks allow you to group specific tasks into their own status checks. This is useful when you want separate pass/fail indicators for different parts of your CI pipeline, such as tests, linting, or deployments.

We recommend not making custom status checks solely for having more granular visibility of results. RWX provides an aggregated view of failures across a run, which is generally better than having to click into multiple status checks individually. However, you may prefer having separate status checks.

You can also use custom status checks to have more flexibility with which tasks are required to succeed based on the branch protection rules that you have configured in your version control platform.

### Single task

To create a custom status check for a single task:

```yaml
on:
  github:
    push:
      status-checks:
        - tasks: unit-tests

```

You can also give it a custom name:


### Multiple tasks

To group multiple tasks into a single status check:

```yaml
on:
  github:
    push:
      status-checks:
        - tasks: [integration-tests, e2e-tests]

```

The custom status check will show as successful only when all specified tasks succeed.

### Combining default and custom

You can configure both the default status check and custom status checks:

```yaml
on:
  github:
    push:
      status-checks:
        default:
          name: CI
        custom:
          - tasks: lint
            name: Linting
          - tasks: [unit-tests, integration-tests]
            name: Tests

```

If you only specify custom status checks (without the `default` key), the default status check remains enabled.

## Configuration reference

### Boolean shorthand

The simplest form enables or disables all status checks:

```yaml
status-checks: true # Enable (default behavior)
status-checks: false # Disable all status checks

```

### Template Expressions

You can use [template expressions](/docs/expressions) for dynamic configuration.

### Default status check options

| Field   | Type                | Default        | Description                                |
| ------- | ------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| enabled | boolean or template | true           | Whether to create the default status check |
| name    | string or template  | auto-generated | Custom display name for the status check   |

### Custom status check options

| Field | Type                 | Required | Description                                           |
| ----- | -------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| tasks | string or string\[\] | Yes      | Task key(s) to include in this status check           |
| name  | string or template   | No       | Custom display name (auto-generated if not specified) |

## Dispatch triggers

[Dispatch triggers](/docs/dispatch-triggers) can report status checks too, but unlike VCS provider events, they're off by default for dispatched runs. Opt in with a `status-checks` block on the trigger:

```yaml
on:
  dispatch:
    key: deploy-application
    status-checks:
      enabled: true
      name: Deploy

```

When enabled, the dispatched run posts a commit status back to the repository for the ref it ran against. `name` sets the label shown on that commit status (or check run).

### Waiting to start manually

When a dispatch trigger uses [start: manually](/docs/dispatch-triggers#start-manually), the run is created in a waiting state until someone starts it. The `start-manually` option in the status checks configuration controls what the status check reports while the run waits:

* `succeeded` (the default) reports the check as successful, so it won't block merges.
* `waiting` keeps the check pending, blocking merges until the run is started.

```yaml
on:
  dispatch:
    key: deploy-application
    start: manually
    status-checks:
      enabled: true
      start-manually: waiting

```

### Dispatch status check options

| Field          | Type                 | Default        | Description                                                       |
| -------------- | -------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| enabled        | boolean or template  | false          | Whether the dispatched run reports a status check                 |
| name           | string or template   | auto-generated | Custom display name for the status check                          |
| start-manually | succeeded or waiting | succeeded      | What the check reports while the run waits to be started manually |

## Behavior

A task that is skipped in RWX but specified in a custom status check will report a failed status check. In the following example, if `unit-tests` does not run, then the "Unit Tests" check will be marked as failed.

```yaml
on:
  github:
    push:
      status-checks:
        - tasks: unit-tests
          name: Unit Tests

```

content.text:
I changed the `.rwx` trigger configs so the duplicate `*.yml (pull request)` checks should stop appearing. I haven't tested it on a pushed PR yet. The changes are uncommitted and not pushed.

**Cause:** RWX adds a default check for every run, named after the file, and your custom named checks (`pytest`, `frontend-deps` and so on) were showing up alongside it.

**Changes:**
- **`frontend.yml`, `tests.yml`, `reflex-build.yml`, `trunk-check.yml`:** I turned off the default check on both the push and pull-request triggers. Only the named checks remain: `frontend-deps`, `pytest`, `reflex-export`, `trunk-check` and `tach-external`.
- **`preview.yml`:** it has no custom check, so I renamed its default check to `RWX: preview`.

`rwx lint` on every file gives only a warning that the package version is outdated. That warning also appears without my changes.

**Needs your check:** the old `RWX: preview.yml (pull request)` check will disappear. If branch protection or the Trunk `merge.required_statuses` setting requires it, you'll need to update that to `RWX: preview`. The screenshot shows "1 expected" check, which may be that one.

I removed the `.yml` from the check names and kept every check. I haven't pushed this to the PR yet, so I haven't seen it on GitHub. `rwx lint` on the changed files reports only the outdated-package-version warning.

The old names came from RWX's default per-run check, which is named after the file. I set an explicit name on each one:

- **`tests.yml`:** the default check is now `RWX: pytest`. I removed the separate custom `pytest` check, since it would have had the same name.
- **`frontend.yml`:** the default check is now `RWX: frontend-deps`, and the separate custom check is removed.
- **`reflex-build.yml`:** the default check is now `RWX: reflex-export`, and the separate custom check is removed.
- **`preview.yml`:** the default check is now `RWX: preview`.
- **`trunk-check.yml`:** the default check is now `RWX: trunk-check-run`. The custom `trunk-check` and `tach-external` checks stay as they were.

**Needs your check:**
- `RWX: trunk-check-run` is a name I picked, because `trunk-check` is already taken by the custom check. Tell me if you want a different name.
- For the three single-task files, the check now reflects the whole run rather than one named task. That is the same thing in practice, since each file runs one job.
- If `.trunk/trunk.yaml` `merge.required_statuses` lists any of the old `.yml` names, update them to the new ones.
